content.text:
**Finding: COMPLIANT (preferred level)** — no redline proposed.

**Why:** The rule's single preferred element — "Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation" — is already met on the face of the Agreement.

- **§5.8 Exclusivity with Respect to the Territory (p0367–p0369)** is directionally in our favour: it binds *Harpoon* and its Affiliates against developing, commercializing or out-licensing Competing Products in the Territory. The 5.8.2 carve-outs are Harpoon-side acquisition/change-of-control exceptions that in fact hand AbbVie extra rights (Confidential Information shut-off, JGC disbandment).
- **§5.1.3(a)–(b) (p0355–p0356)** are exclusive *grants to AbbVie*, including against Harpoon itself — a benefit, not a restraint.
- **§5.6.1 (p0363)** retains rights for Harpoon only outside the licensed scope and is expressly "subject to Section 5.8."
- AbbVie is affirmatively free to use third parties: distributor appointments "in its sole discretion" (§5.4), co-promotion with any Person or Third Party (§5.5), and first right to take third-party in-licences (§5.9.2).

Targeted searches for requirements/sole-supply language, third-party procurement bars, and any "AbbVie shall not … Competing Product" restraint returned nothing binding our client. Consistent with the detection guidance, exclusivity granted to the Customer is not a deviation, and the Harpoon non-compete is left to NONCOMPETE rather than double-flagged here.
